thread:
caroline: FYI ACME (acct acme-inc) just opened an escalation — p99s jumped to ~6s for a set of requests against their Dedicated pool eu-west-1-dedicated-42 starting ~08:15 UTC. They see user-facing errors. Can oncall pick up?
leo: I'm on it, tagging @tara. Do we have alerts/graphs?
tara: Getting the live dashboard now. p95 ~1.2s but p99 up to 6.1s, correlates with a burst at 08:14:30. CPU on several GPUs low, queue length spiked.
jamal: infra alert fired: autoscaler attach lag increased, scaleups queued. infra-bot shows attach backlog of 28 for pool eu-west-1-dedicated-42.
infra-bot: alert: autoscaler_attach_backlog >= 20 (window 5m). current_backlog=28. recent_scaleups: 2 -> 3 nodes in last 3m.
leo: Any recent deploys to the attach/image? @deploy-bot?
deploy-bot: deploy: image-registry/redwood/runtime:2026-03-17-1212 rolled to eu-west-1-provisioner ~07:55 UTC. No rollback noted.
jamal: I see a spike of concurrent hot-attaches from a few high-priority customers, fairshare pushed them into the same pool. That may cause container/driver init thundering herd.
tara: Repro steps from support to reproduce latency: curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <ACME_KEY>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"redwood-dedicated-v2","input":"<500-token prompt>","max_tokens":256}'  — returns 504 or 5-6s sometimes.
leo: Looking at provisioner logs: many Attach RPCs timing out at 10s, then retry loops. Sample: ```ERROR provisioner: attach timeout id=attach-abc123 duration=10.02s pool=eu-west-1-dedicated-42 reason="image-pull-slow"```
jamal: Image pulls were slower due to registry throttling (burst from demo environment). A handful of nodes fell behind warmup. Cache miss for KV-store prefix also increased upstream latency.
caroline: Customer asks for ETA and workaround — they are high priority.
tara: Immediate mitigations: 1) Increase min_pool size for that dedicated pool to +2 to cover burst. 2) Temporarily route ACME traffic to a warm standby pool eu-west-1-hot-standby (hosted-backed) while we stabilize. 3) Kick prewarm on new nodes.
leo: I'll run commands: ```infractl pool update --name eu-west-1-dedicated-42 --min-instances 4``` then ```infractl prewarm --pool eu-west-1-dedicated-42 --count 3```
leo: Done. min-instances bumped, prewarm triggered. infra-bot: scale request acknowledged.
infra-bot: action: requested scale up +2 warm instances to eu-west-1-dedicated-42. estimated_ready=80s.
jamal: While nodes come up, I'll set a targeted routing rule for ACME to fallback to hosted low-latency model: ```routingctl override --acct acme-inc --route /v1/generate -> redwood-hosted-lowlatency``` — that will preserve SLA until pool healthy.
caroline: Applied. ACME confirms reduced error rate and p99 back to ~1.8s for routed traffic. :white_check_mark:
tara: Post-mortem notes so far: root causes = registry throttling causing image-pull slow → attach timeouts → attach retry surge → attach backlog → queueing at front-end. Contributing factor = min_pool configured too low for sudden VIP bursts + no per-customer isolation.
leo: Actions: (A) Increase default min_pool for dedicated pools with >2 VIP customers, (B) implement short randomized attach jitter in provisioner, (C) add registry pull circuit-breaker and proactive image pre-push to regional caches, (D) add alert for sustained image-pull-latency >2s. Assigned: leo(A,B), jamal(C), tara(D).
jamal: I'll also add a short-term compensating policy: when attach_backlog > 15 for 2m, auto-route high-urgency customers to warm standby pools automatically. Will open PR.
caroline: Customer notified of workaround and expected longer-term fixes. They requested a follow-up within 24h.
leo: Logging follow-up: collect attach RPC traces from 08:10-08:30, provisioner node logs, and registry metrics. I'll drop artifacts in #support/1823456789 for postmortem.
tara: Marking incident as "active - mitigated". If p99 remains >3s after new nodes join, we escalate to eng-runtime.
caroline: Thanks team, I'll keep ACME updated. :pray:
